content: 【大纪元2026年11月16日讯】11月12日，是孙中山先生一百六十周年诞辰。北京高规格举行纪念大会。习近平在讲话中声称，中国共产党人是孙中山先生革命事业“最坚定的支持者、最忠诚的合作者、最忠实的继承者”，并强调孙中山坚定维护国家统一。 在我看来，习近平给中共戴上孙中山“最忠实的继承者”这顶桂冠，纯属对历史的无耻篡改。 思想体系：三民主义与共产主义 南辕北辙 孙中山毕生奋斗的思想旗帜，是民族、民权、民生三民主义。民族主义追求的是推翻帝制、建立独立的民族国家；民权主义的核心，是“主权在民”，要建立一个有宪法、有国会、有选举、有言论自由的共和政体；民生主义主张平均地权、节制资本，是在私有制和市场经济的框架内追求社会公平。孙中山晚年虽然提出“联俄容共”，但他接纳的，是苏俄的援助与合作，而非马克思主义的国家学说。 共产主义则是一套完全不同的理论与实践：阶级斗争、无产阶级专政、消灭私有制、党的绝对领导。这套学说恰恰是孙中山民权主义所要防止的东西。孙中山在《三民主义》演讲中反复告诫：民权不是从天而降的恩赐，而是要靠制度来保障的。他设想的五权宪法、国民大会、地方自治，无一不是以限制权力、还政于民为出发点。以阶级专政取代主权在民，以一党永久执政取代宪政共和，这与三民主义在根本处是对立的。习近平说二者是“继承”关系，在思想史上是站不住脚的。 历史进程：继承者，还是终结者？ 看历史事实，更能说明问题。 辛亥革命之后，中国曾有过民初的国会选举、多党竞争与新闻自由，虽然幼稚、混乱，却是共和的萌芽。1927年之后国共分道，1949年中共建政，中国走上了一条与孙中山宪政蓝图完全不同的道路。反右、大跃进、文革，国家权力不受任何制约，公民权利荡然无存——孙中山毕生追求的“民权”，在这段历史中不是被继承，而是被悬置乃至终结了。 有人说，中共完成了国家统一与工业化，这是对孙中山遗志的继承。但孙中山的遗志从来不只是“富国强兵”，更是“还政于民”。《建国方略》里铁路港口的蓝图可以实现，宪政的蓝图却恰恰是至今没有兑现的那一部分。只继承建设蓝图，不继承权力制衡的设计，这叫选择性继承，谈不上“最忠实”。 两岸问题的叙事也值得注意。孙中山逝世时，中华民国已经存在，今天台湾地区继承的，正是当年那部宪法和五院体制的余绪。北京以“孙中山维护国家统一”来论证统一主张，却回避了一个更基本的问题：孙中山主张的统一，是在共和宪政框架内的统一，而不是以专政消灭共和的统一。 为什么偏偏是孙中山？ 那么，为什么中共如此执著地宣称自己是孙中山的传人？ 原因不难理解。 第一，孙中山是两岸与海内外华人最大公约数的政治符号，谁掌握了对他的解释权，谁就占据了正统叙事的制高点。 第二，中共的合法性叙事需要一条从辛亥到今天的历史主线——把1949年说成辛亥革命的“完成”，就能把百年历史写成一个连续的、必然的剧本。 第三，“继承者”的说法，能把孙中山宪政理想中那些至今未兑现的承诺，收编进自己的话语体系，使其失去独立的批判力量。 但符号的借用，代替不了思想的检验。判断“继承”与否，标准不应是纪念大会的规格，而应看基本理念是否相续、制度设计是否相承、历史走向是否相合。以此衡量，三民主义与共产主义、宪政与专政、主权在民与党的领导，处处相悖，何谈“最忠实”？ 孙中山留给中国的最宝贵遗产，不是某一项工程蓝图，早日而是他的信念：中国应当成为一个主权在民的现代共和国。真正纪念孙中山，最好的方式不是把他的名字写进纪念讲话，更不是给自己带上“最忠实的继承者”的桂冠，而是实现他的遗愿，早日把中国建成一个真正的民主宪政国家。恰恰在这个最根本的问题上，中共建政后的所作所为，无一不是在开历史的倒车，与孙中山的遗愿背道而驰，有如此厚这种颜无耻的“最忠实的继承者”吗？

title: Hong Kong whistleblower of student app scandal charged with doxxing
zh_title: 香港学生应用程序丑闻举报人被控人肉搜索
summary: 一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。一个
content:
一名香港女子因质疑一名中学生获奖应用程序的合法性而引发学术诚信争议，她被指控人肉搜索。郑海莉.照片：Hailey Cheng，来自 Facebook。根据周三的法庭文件，海莉·程 (Hailey Cheng) 面临四项未经数据主体同意披露个人数据并造成特定伤害的指控。曾就读于香港城市大学、现就读于纽约哥伦比亚大学的郑女士当天在Threads上表示，该案已在法庭上提及，并已获准保释。根据指控书，程被指控披露四名未透露姓名的人（X、Y、Z 和 A）的个人数据。据称，她这样做的目的是为了对这些人或其家人造成特定伤害，或者不顾后果地考虑是否会造成伤害。程被指控在未经她同意的情况下披露了“X”的中英文全名、她的年龄、学校、学年、家庭关系、社交媒体资料、照片、居住区域、资格和行程。据称，她还披露了其他三人的个人信息，包括姓名、照片和家庭关系。 Y 的出生日期被泄露，Z 的住所被泄露，A 的社交媒体资料被泄露。
周三，郑在东区裁判法院出庭，在首席裁判官苏泽豪面前出庭，无需答辩。裁判官批准了辩方休庭寻求法律意见的请求，以及控方为受害者申请匿名令的申请。案件押后至12月23日审理。文件显示，郑以3,000港元现金保释。去年六月，Cheng 担心 MediSafe（一款荣获多项奖项的药物处方应用程序）实际上并非由中学生 Clarisse Poon 制作，引发了病毒式的学术诚信丑闻。一家名为 AI Health Studio 的美国软件开发公司后来表示，该应用程序是受潘的母亲委托开发的，并且该应用程序未经其同意就提交给了比赛。早些时候被捕 这名大学生二月份在社交媒体上表示，她因举报事件而被捕。在八月份的一份声明中，她说她拒绝保释并被无条件释放。拒绝更新保释是指一个人拒绝接受延长保释期限并要求警方正式指控或释放他们的程序。如果出现进一步证据，警方仍可以稍后重新逮捕并指控嫌疑人。东部裁判法院。照片：何凯莉/HKFP。四月，程面临亲北京支持者要求被城大开除的呼吁。
香港编程协会 Facebook 群组的一名匿名成员当月发布了请愿书，敦促“香港庞大的蓝营”分享该请愿书。请愿书还表示，签名者将与警方、国家安全部门和中联办等当局联系，要求将她驱逐。据当地媒体报道，著名肝病专家 Ronnie Poon 和学生家长 Roberta Pang 在 8 月打破沉默，表示他们的女儿将归还与 MediSafe 相关的所有奖项。

【原文 English Original】
A Hong Kong woman who sparked a viral academic integrity controversy after questioning the legitimacy of a secondary student’s award-winning app has been charged with doxxing. Hailey Cheng. Photo: Hailey Cheng, via Facebook. Hailey Cheng faces four counts of disclosing personal data without a data subject’s consent causing specified harm, according to court documents dated Wednesday. Cheng, a former student at the City University of Hong Kong now admitted to Columbia University in New York, said on Threads the same day that the case had been mentioned in court and that she was granted bail . According to the charge sheet, Cheng was charged with disclosing personal data of four unnamed people referred to as X, Y, Z, and A. She allegedly did so with an intent to cause specified harm to those people or their family members, or being reckless as to whether the harm would be caused. Cheng was accused of disclosing the full English and Chinese names of “X,” her age, school, school year, family relationships, social media profiles, photos, living area, qualifications, and itinerary without her consent. She also allegedly disclosed personal information of the other three people, including their names, photos, and family relationships. The person known as Y had her date of birth disclosed, while Z had his residence leaked, and the individual known as A had her social media profile disclosed. Cheng appeared before Chief Magistrate Victor So at the Eastern Magistrates’ Courts on Wednesday and was not required to enter a plea. The magistrate granted the defence’s request for an adjournment to seek legal advice and the prosecution’s application for an anonymity order for the victims. The case was adjourned to December 23. According to the document, Cheng was released on a HK$3,000 cash bail. Last June, Cheng raised concerns that MediSafe – a medication prescription app that won multiple awards – was not actually made by secondary school student Clarisse Poon, triggering a viral academic integrity scandal. A US-based software development company called AI Health Studio later said it was commissioned by Poon’s mother to build the app, and that the app was submitted to competitions without its consent. Earlier arrest The university student said on social media in February that she had been arrested in relation to the whistleblowing incident. In an August statement, she said that she refused bail and was released unconditionally. Refusing to renew bail is a procedure where a person declines to accept an extension of bail terms and requires the police to either formally charge or release them. The police can still re-arrest and charge the suspect later if further evidence emerges. Eastern Magistrates’ Courts. Photo: Kelly Ho/HKFP. In April, Cheng faced calls from pro-Beijing supporters to be expelled from CityU. An anonymous member of a Facebook group for the Hong Kong Programming Society posted the petition that month urging “Hong Kong’s vast blue camp” to share it. The petition also said that signatories would be in touch with the authorities, including the police, its National Security Department, and Beijing’s Liaison Office to demand her expulsion. Renowned liver disease specialist Ronnie Poon and Roberta Pang, the student’s parents, broke their silence in August, saying their daughter would return all the awards associated with MediSafe, according to local media  reports .

title: Hong Kong gov’t seeks HK$19.8 billion from legislature to fund early Ngau Tam Mei development
zh_title: 香港政府向立法会寻求198亿港元资助牛潭尾早期开发
summary: 香港政府正在寻求立法会批准为牛潭尾早期开发阶段提供 198 亿港元的资金，牛潭尾是庞大的北方都会项目的一个主要区域。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，一幅横幅展示了牛潭尾的新开发区，新田大学城的一个校园区将坐落于此。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局及土木工程拓展署在周二向立法会提交的文件中估计牛潭尾新D区的工地平整及基础设施工程
content:
香港政府正在寻求立法会批准为牛潭尾早期开发阶段提供 198 亿港元的资金，牛潭尾是庞大的北方都会项目的一个主要区域。 2026 年 10 月 30 日，一幅横幅展示了牛潭尾的新开发区，新田大学城的一个校园区将坐落于此。照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。发展局及土木工程拓展署在周二向立法会提交的文件中估计，牛潭尾新发展区的工地平整及基础设施工程将耗资约198亿港元。根据该部门的预测，该地区占地约 130 公顷，将创造约 26,000 个就业岗位，并容纳 35,400 至 38,500 人。新田大学城是北部都会项目规划的三个高等教育集群之一，位于牛潭尾，占地约52公顷。该地区的五公顷土地已预留给香港科技大学管理的香港第三所医学院。政府表示，医学院周围约10公顷的土地将被开发为综合医院，以支持研究并为未来的北方都市居民提供服务。
牛潭尾开发区约一半（66公顷）是私人土地，政府估计大约有1,300户家庭和120家企业需要被驱逐，才能为该项目让路。油潭尾村入口，2025年1月25日。该村庄位于牛潭尾新发展区内，村民将从明年开始被驱逐。资料照片：Kyle Lam/HKFP。政府称，该项目将影响约5.7公顷农田、4.1公顷鱼塘和1个养鸡场。工地平整和基础设施工程预计将于 2034 年基本完成，居民最早可于 2033 年搬入。当局计划建设政府和社区设施以及休闲区，但尚未明确时间表。 2021 年宣布的北方都会项目计划将约 300 平方公里（约占城市面积的三分之一）改造成香港与深圳边境的创新和技术中心。另请参阅：科技城到大学城：为什么香港北部都会区将重点从高科技转向高等教育牛潭尾新发展区位于北部都会区项目设想的核心“创新科技区”内，该区还将包括专业服务和物流中心以及旅游和保护设施。发展区内的油潭尾村的居民将于明年起被驱逐。

【原文 English Original】
The Hong Kong government is seeking the Legislative Council’s approval of HK$19.8 billion in funding for the early development phase in Ngau Tam Mei, a major area in the sprawling Northern Metropolis project. A banner shows the new development area in Ngau Tam Mei, where one of the campus areas of the San Tin University Town will be located, October 30, 2026. Photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. In a paper submitted to the Legislative Council on Tuesday, the Development Bureau and the Civil Engineering and Development Department estimated that site formation and infrastructure works in the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area would cost about HK$19.8 billion. The area, spanning about 130 hectares, will create around 26,000 jobs and house a population between 35,400 and 38,500 people, according to the department’s forecasts. The San Tin University Town, one of three higher education clusters planned in the Northern Metropolis project, will cover about 52 hectares in Ngau Tam Mei. Five hectares of that area has been reserved for the city’s third medical school, which will be run by the Hong Kong University of Science and Technology. Around 10 hectares surrounding the medical school will be developed into a general hospital to support research and provide services for future Northern Metropolis residents, the government said. About half of the Ngau Tam Mei development area – 66 hectares – is private land, and the government estimates that roughly 1,300 households and 120 businesses need to be evicted to make way for the project. The entrance to Yau Tam Mei Tsuen, on January 25, 2025. The village sits within the Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area and villagers are set for eviction from next year. File photo: Kyle Lam/HKFP. The project will affect about 5.7 hectares of farmland, 4.1 hectares of fish pond, and one chicken farm, the government said. Site formation and infrastructure works is estimated to be largely completed by 2034, while residents can move in as early as 2033. Authorities plan to build government and community facilities and leisure areas, but have not yet specified a timeline. The Northern Metropolis project, announced in 2021, is set to transform about 300 square kilometres – roughly a third of the city’s territory – into an innovation and technology hub along Hong Kong’s border with Shenzhen. See also: Technopole to University Towns: Why Hong Kong’s Northern Metropolis shifted focus from hi-tech to higher ed The Ngau Tam Mei New Development Area sits within a core “innovation and technology zone” envisioned under the Northern Metropolis project, which will also encompass a professional services and logistics hub as well as tourism and conservation facilities. Residents of Yau Tam Mei Tsuen, a village within the development area, will be evicted from next year .

title: Beijing bolsters South China Sea push with new island runway: analysts
zh_title: 北京通过新岛屿跑道加强南海推进：分析人士
summary: 根据专家和法新社看到的卫星图像，中国正在有争议的南海另一个岛屿上修建一条跑道，这可能会大大加强其在战略水道上的军事足迹。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 10 月 17 日拍摄的讲义卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁上的一个港口的基础。照片：星球实验室/法新社。北京声称对南海大部分地区拥有主权，尽管国际裁决认为其主张没有法律依据，而且与几个国家经常发生对抗
content:
根据专家和法新社看到的卫星图像，中国正在有争议的南海另一个岛屿上修建一条跑道，这可能会大大加强其在战略水道上的军事足迹。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 10 月 17 日拍摄的讲义卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁上的一个港口的基础。照片：星球实验室/法新社。北京声称对南海大部分地区拥有主权，尽管国际裁决认为其主张没有法律依据，而且与几个东南亚国家就西沙群岛和南沙群岛的控制权经常发生对抗。这两个岛链基本上都是由珊瑚礁和露头组成，但分析人士表示，中国一直在稳步填海造地和建设基础设施，以获得对海洋的军事控制权。美国战略与国际研究中心（CSIS）和洛伊研究所在最近的详细报告中援引卫星图像称，北京去年年底开始在西沙群岛羚羊礁进行大规模疏浚和填海造地，中国、越南和台湾均声称对该群岛拥有主权。洛伊研究所报告的作者洛厄尔·鲍蒂斯塔告诉法新社，中国在 10 个月内将西沙群岛的珊瑚礁从最小的西沙群岛前哨基地之一转变为可以与最大的环礁相媲美的岛屿。
羚羊礁上近三公里的跑道将是北京在西沙群岛的第二条跑道，与南沙群岛和海南岛上的基础设施一起，有助于“建立一个跨越大海的跑道、港口和传感器的综合网络”，包蒂斯塔说。1974年，中国和越南在西沙群岛发生了一场短暂但血腥的小冲突。70多名越南士兵被杀，从那时起，中国实际上控制了这些岛屿。据战略与国际研究中心称，该跑道的大小与西沙群岛永兴岛和南沙群岛其他三个机场的跑道相似。分析人士表示，羚羊角沿西北-东南轴线约六公里，可能成为中国在南海最重要的前哨基地之一，有可能帮助北京在发生冲突时限制美国及其盟国海军的进入。中国表示，西沙群岛的开发是出于民用目的，并补充说，西沙群岛的居民人口较少，主要是渔民。外交部发言人三月份表示，中国在该岛的填海造地活动是“必要的建设”，目的是“改善岛上的生活和工作条件，发展当地经济”。运输机、轰炸机 在地球成像公司 Planet Labs 9 月份拍摄的照片中，清晰可见一个看起来像跑道的结构。
这些图像是日本情报公司 Deep Dive 最近报告的一部分，法新社也看到了这些图像。这张由 Planet Labs PBC 于 2026 年 11 月 8 日拍摄的分发卫星图像显示了南海西沙群岛有争议的羚羊礁。照片：星球实验室/法新社。 Deep Dive 主任、前驻中国武官 Bonji Ohara 在报告中表示，该结构不仅能够容纳战斗机，还能够容纳更大型的飞机，包括运输机、空中加油机和轰炸机。他说，新跑道可能会让中国更接近实现“对整个南海的完全控制”。 CSIS 表示，Antelope 可以增强中国传感能力的覆盖范围

【原文 English Original】
China is building a runway on another island in the disputed South China Sea that could significantly strengthen its military footprint in the strategic waterway, according to experts and satellite images seen by AFP. This handout satellite image taken by Planet Labs PBC on October 17, 2026 shows the foundations of a harbour on the disputed Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. Photo: Planet Labs/AFP. Beijing claims most of the South China Sea, despite an international ruling that its assertion has no legal basis, and confrontations have occurred regularly with  several Southeast Asian nations over control of the Paracel and Spratly islands. Both island chains are essentially made up of reefs and outcrops, but analysts say China has been steadily reclaiming land and building infrastructure to gain military control of the sea. Beijing late last year began large-scale dredging and reclaiming land at Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands, which are claimed by China, Vietnam and Taiwan, the Center for Strategic and International Studies (CSIS) and the Lowy Institute said in recent detailed reports, citing satellite images. Lowell Bautista, author of the Lowy Institute report, told AFP that China transformed the reef in 10 months from one of its smallest Paracel outposts into an island that can rival its largest atoll. The nearly three-kilometre runway on Antelope Reef would be Beijing’s second in the Paracels and — together with infrastructure on the Spratly Islands and on Hainan island — helps “create an integrated network of runways, harbours and sensors stretching across the sea”, Bautista said. China and Vietnam fought a brief but bloody skirmish over the Paracels in 1974. More than 70 Vietnamese soldiers were killed and China has had de facto control over the islands since then. The runway is a similar size to an airstrip on the Paracels’ Woody Island and three others across the Spratlys, according to CSIS. Analysts say Antelope — which is around six kilometres along its northwest-southeast axis — could become one of China’s most important outposts in the South China Sea, potentially helping Beijing limit the access of US and allied naval forces in the event of conflict. China says the development of the Paracel Islands, which it adds have a small resident population of mostly fishers, is for civilian purposes. A spokesperson for the foreign ministry said in March that China’s land reclamation activities there are “necessary construction” for “improving living and working conditions on the islands and growing the local economy”. Transport planes, bombers A structure that appears to be a runway is clearly visible in photos taken in September by Earth imaging company Planet Labs. The images were reviewed as part of a recent report by Japanese intelligence firm Deep Dive and were also seen by AFP. This handout satellite image taken by Planet Labs PBC on November 8, 2026 shows the disputed Antelope Reef in the Paracel Islands in the South China Sea. Photo: Planet Labs/AFP. Deep Dive director Bonji Ohara, a former defence attache in China, said in the report that the structure would be able to handle not just fighter jets but also larger aircraft, including transport planes, aerial refuelling tankers and bombers. The new runway could potentially bring China closer to achieving “full control over the entire South China Sea”, he said. The CSIS has said that Antelope could enhance the reach of Chinese sensing capabilities closer to Vietnam’s shores and help expand its military capacity in an area of the northern South China Sea which is close to major shipping lanes. Antelope Reef’s runway is expected to be operational by mid-2027, although other analysts were more cautious about its significance. The runway and harbour will “add additional capacity and resilience to the facility that enable China’s military and paramilitary operations in the South China Sea,” Harrison Pretat, deputy director at CSIS’s Asia Maritime Transparency Initiative, told AFP. But “Southeast Asian claimants have still largely maintained access to offshore resources and occupy their own outposts,” he said. Limited pushback Nevertheless, Pretat warned that “international attention and pushback… has been far less than might be expected given the scale and significance” of construction, due in part “to distraction from other global crises”. “Regional countries…along with the United States and the international community, should be speaking with a stronger voice against island building and other attempts to permanently alter conditions in disputed areas,” he said. Vietnam in August called construction at Antelope Reef “completely illegal” and demanded “such activities cease immediately”. And in October, Australian Defence Minister Richard Marles said that China’s military build-up was creating a “condition of pressure” in Southeast Asia, and urged allies and partners to deepen cooperation. But Hunter Marston of the Lowy Institute told AFP that “ASEAN (member states) will never be capable of communicating with one voice” due partly to their different views of China. A crew member of the China Coast Guard vessel 5205 removes the cover of a 70 mm cannon and aims it toward the BRP Teresa Magbanua near Second Thomas Shoal in the South China Sea in August 2022. File photo: Philippine Coast Guard. US ally the Philippines has been engaged in years of confrontations with China over disputed areas of the sea, and Filipino and Chinese ships have engaged in repeated confrontations in recent years, some leading to collisions and injuries. Ohara said that Beijing views the sea as “a sanctuary… where it does not want foreign powers to enter in the event of a contingency” in the region. “While it will not restrict freedom of navigation in peacetime, if some incident occurs, China intends to prevent not only US naval forces but also those of its allies — for example, Australian submarines — from entering,” he said.

title: Trump seeks diplomatic gains on Asia tour as Putin arrives in China
zh_title: 普京抵达中国，特朗普寻求亚洲之行的外交收获
summary: 俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周三抵达中国，准备与中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行峰会。在国内选举惨败后，特朗普正在亚洲之行寻求外交成果。 2026 年 11 月 17 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达尼诺·阿基诺国际机场，出席在马尼拉举行的第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会，他挥舞着美国和菲律宾国旗。照片：Eloisa Lopez/法新社。特朗普周二在菲律宾与所谓的“四方”国家和地区的领导人会面。
content:
俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京周三抵达中国，准备与中国国家主席习近平和美国总统唐纳德·特朗普举行峰会。在国内选举惨败后，特朗普正在亚洲之行寻求外交成果。 2026 年 11 月 17 日，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普抵达尼诺·阿基诺国际机场，出席在马尼拉举行的第 49 届东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 峰会，他挥舞着美国和菲律宾国旗。照片：Eloisa Lopez/法新社。特朗普周二在菲律宾与所谓的四方国家领导人会面，并表示他计划在下一站中国深圳举行的亚太经济合作组织（APEC）峰会上与普京和朝鲜金正恩进行一对一会谈。特朗普在与四国领导人印度纳伦德拉·莫迪、日本首相高市早苗和澳大利亚总理安东尼·阿尔巴内塞合影时对记者说：“如果有的话，我会这么做。”他补充说，朝鲜金正恩“希望”在中国会面，几小时前北京表示没有关于两人会面的信息。另请参阅：中国称习近平、特朗普和普京将在深圳峰会上讨论“世界和平” 特朗普在东南亚国家联盟 (ASEAN) 11 名成员国峰会上举行的四方会议是他 2025 年 1 月重新掌权以来该安全联盟的首次会议。
分析人士称，虽然主要旨在制衡中国的地区影响力的四方会谈在深化协调方面取得了悄然进展，但周二会议的时间很短，这意味着会议不可能超越寒暄。在马尼拉，特朗普在机场停机坪上受到了游行乐队和仪仗队的欢迎，而在其他地方，约有 2000 名示威者与警察对峙，他们举着写着“特朗普现在下台”和“拒绝 Pax Silica”的横幅——指的是美国的供应这一连锁倡议在菲律宾引起了分歧。关税、芯片和稀土 虽然东盟领导人花了三天时间努力解决一系列地区问题，但特朗普正在进行的关税闪电战的幽灵已经隐约可见。中国总理李强周一猛烈抨击了他所谓的“单边主义和保护主义的逆流”，同时宣传了北京与欧盟不断扩大的贸易。巴西总统路易斯·伊纳西奥·卢拉·达席尔瓦和加拿大总统马克·卡尼在贸易问题上也唱出了类似的调子，两人都明确表示需要摆脱对美国市场的依赖。加拿大总理马克·卡尼于 2026 年 10 月 17 日在深圳与中国国家主席习近平握手。照片：马克·卡尼，来自 Threads。周二，好斗的特朗普在与北京的贸易战中丝毫没有放松，他表示美国将“在10个月内”在稀土产量上赶上中国。 “我们正在以前所未有的水平生产稀土。
他们说，我们将在 10 个月内抓住他们。”他说。在特朗普抵达马尼拉前几个小时，华盛顿宣布了有关先进人工智能芯片转让的新规则，此举可能会激怒东盟成员国。向新加坡、马来西亚、泰国和印度尼西亚运送高端芯片的公司现在需要特殊许可证，因为据说这些国家代表着“高于正常的转移风险”。新加坡回应称，它正在探索为总部位于新加坡的公司提供“可信准入”的方法。特朗普将于周三在总统府会见菲律宾领导人费迪南德·马科斯，然后前往。

【原文 English Original】
Russian President Vladimir Putin on Wednesday arrived in China ahead of a summit with his Chinese counterpart Xi Jinping and US President Donald Trump, who is on an Asian tour in search of diplomatic gains after a bruising election defeat back home. US President Donald Trump waves US and Philippine flags upon arriving at the Ninoy Aquino International Airport to attend the 49th Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) Summit in Manila on November 17, 2026. Photo: Eloisa Lopez/AFP. Trump was in the Philippines on Tuesday for a meeting with the leaders of the so-called Quad countries and said he was eyeing one-on-one talks with Putin and North Korea’s Kim Jong Un at his next stop, the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in China’s Shenzhen. “If it’s available, I would do that,” Trump told reporters as he stood for photos with fellow Quad leaders Narendra Modi of India, Japanese Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi and Australia’s Anthony Albanese. He added that North Korea’s Kim “would like” to meet in China, hours after Beijing said it had no information about an encounter between the two. See also: China says Xi, Trump, Putin to discuss ‘world peace’ at Shenzhen summit Trump’s Quad meeting at the 11-member Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) summit was the security alliance’s first since his January 2025 return to power. While the Quad –- broadly aimed at counterbalancing China’s regional influence — has quietly progressed in deepening coordination, the short time allotted for Tuesday’s meeting meant it was unlikely to extend beyond pleasantries, according to analysts. While Trump was greeted in Manila by a marching band and honour guard on the airport tarmac, elsewhere some 2,000 demonstrators faced off with police, carrying banners reading “Trump out now” and “Reject Pax Silica” — a reference to a US supply chain initiative that has divided opinion in the Philippines. Tariffs, chips and rare earths While ASEAN leaders have spent three days grappling with a raft of regional issues, the spectre of Trump’s ongoing tariff blitz has loomed large. Chinese Premier Li Qiang on Monday slammed what he called a “countercurrent of unilateralism and protectionism” while touting Beijing’s own expanding trade with the bloc. Brazilian President Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva and Canada’s Mark Carney sang a similar tune on trade, with both explicitly citing a need to wean themselves off dependence on the US market. Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney shakes hands with China’s Xi Jinping in Shenzhen on October 17, 2026. Photo: Mark Carney, via Threads. On Tuesday, a combative Trump showed no let-up in his trade war with Beijing, saying the United States would catch China in rare earths production “within 10 months”. “We are making rare earths at a level that we’ve never made before. We’re going to catch them within 10 months, they say,” he said. Hours before Trump touched down in Manila, Washington announced new rules on the transfer of advanced AI chips, a move that could potentially rankle ASEAN members. Companies shipping high-end chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand and Indonesia will now require a special licence, as the countries were said to represent a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion”. Singapore responded by saying it was now exploring ways to facilitate “trusted access” for firms based in the city-state. Pax Silica Trump will meet Philippine leader Ferdinand Marcos at the presidential palace on Wednesday before heading to Shenzhen. Hayley Channer, economic security director at the Sydney-based United States Studies Centre, said the Manila visit was “likely because the US is trying to further its Pax Silica initiative, to build a complete mine-to-chip supply chain”. Aimed at countering China’s dominance in semiconductors and rare earths, the initiative has been the focus of months of protests in the Philippines, as its flagship 1,620-hectare (about 4,000-acre) AI manufacturing hub north of Manila threatens to displace Indigenous families. “We are gathered here today to call for the stop of Pax Silica and to save the lands of the Filipino people,” Mariposa, a 21-year-old drag queen, told AFP at Tuesday’s protest while wearing a long black cape emblazoned with the words “Pax Silica Sashay Away!” Pax Silica signing ceremony. Photo: US Department of State. US Ambassador Lee Lipton said last week that a long-rumoured deal signing for the site would not take place during the president’s visit. As the ASEAN summit came to a close on Tuesday, President Marcos touted the bloc’s signing of a Digital Economy Framework Agreement — aimed at streamlining digital trade and cross-border payments — as its signature achievement. But he also acknowledged the failure to deliver a “Code of Conduct” on the South China Sea between ASEAN and China during the Philippines’ year as bloc chair. Marcos told reporters that “85-90 percent of it has actually been done”, leaving the ball in Singapore’s court when it takes the ASEAN reins next year.

title: 當 AI 給出答案，我們還期待新聞機構做什麼？

content: 看到一則新聞，想弄清楚事情的來龍去脈；朋友傳來一個聳動的說法，不確定是真是假；某個議題討論了好幾天，想知道大家究竟在爭論什麼⋯⋯以前我們會去Google一下，現在你會打開搜尋引擎，還是直接問 AI？ 數年前，我們在討論的是社群媒體的崛起：大家從主動打開新聞網站，轉向在社群平台上接觸新聞；那媒體該如何跟上這個變化，吸引用戶進來自己的門戶？一但AI出現後，連這個問題也被淘汰了，因為把新聞貼給 AI，就能請它解釋背景、整理不同立場，看不懂的地方，還可以請 AI 用簡單的方式說明。「零點擊搜尋」早已是常態，媒體甚至難以追求讓讀者點進來讀。 科技帶來的改變，不只是接收資訊的管道。AI 整理好的回答，也可能讓我們不再點開原始報導，也未必知道答案裡的資訊，是誰採訪、查證和寫下的。那麼，未來專業的新聞機構到底還有甚麼角色？我們還需要記者和編輯做哪些事？ 今年，端傳媒在年度用戶調研裡，邀請大家一起思索這個假想：如果有一天，AI 已經能準確回答任何議題的任何問題，而且不再出錯，專業新聞機構還需要存在嗎？ 結果是，幾乎所有人都說：需要。近 99% 填問卷的人表示，專業的新聞機構仍需存在。 那麼，大家期待新聞機構做些什麼？ 期待到現場發現問題，也在事件過後持續追問 即使假設 AI 能準確回答問題，差不多每兩個填問卷的人，就有一個認為，值得追問的問題、需要記錄的事件，還是得靠專業媒體人到現場、持續追問。這是最多人的選擇，其次才是採編理念、操守與責任，以及個性化回應以外的新視角。 你有過這樣的經驗嗎？當一件事發生時，接連讀了好幾篇新聞，過一陣子想知道後來怎麼了，卻找不到後續。 近半填問卷的人，就遇到了類似的情況。信任的媒體雖然報導了自己關心的議題，卻零零散散、不夠持續；也有人幾乎找不到相關報導，只好自己東拼西湊。 香港的獨立書店，是端一直追蹤的議題。從2016年銅鑼灣書店事件，到近年獨立書店被搜查、結束營業，同樣是書店新聞，每一次採訪面對的處境卻不一樣。 搜查之後，書店還能繼續營業嗎，結束結束營業後，經營者又去了哪裡？新聞熱度退去，這些問題未必已經有了答案。 「追蹤長期議題」也是許多人閱讀端的原因。一則留言寫道：「當傳統媒體在某個社會事件的現場完全絕跡的時候，希望端仍然可以給出一定的調查與報道。」 另一位則直言：「多去现场吧，我不想再看文献综述了。」 面對真假未明的消息，將近一半的人先找信任的媒體確認 聽到一則真假未明的聳動消息時，讀者真的會先問AI嗎？我們發現，將近一半填問卷的人，會先看看信任的媒體有沒有報導；如果沒有，就暫時當作還沒確認。有人會在感興趣時自己找一手來源，也有人簡單搜尋一下，再問 AI。 重大事件發生時，不少人也會主動找端。在社群蓬勃發展的現在，當消息一則接一則，說法五花八門，這時大家最想知道的，往往是哪些事已經確認、哪些還不能下結論。 這是今天大家面對消息的方式。這也是約三成填問卷的人，仍把採編理念、操守與責任，列為新聞機構需要存在的首要理由。 讀一篇報導，可以知道它訪問了誰、用了什麼資料，也知道哪些問題還沒查清楚。如果後來發現有錯，還能找到更正，以及更正的原因。答案之外，這些交代也影響我們願不願意相信新聞的真實性。 而確認消息是真的之後，下一個問題往往才剛開始：它為什麼會發生？ 比起知道發生什麼，大家更想理解為什麼 十個填問卷的人裡，有八個以上追蹤新聞，是為了弄懂事情為什麼發生、背後是什麼樣的結構，比想知道「究竟發生了什麼」的人更多。也有人想確認有人認真看待這件事，或希望重要的事被記錄下來、不被遺忘。 香港大埔宏福苑火災發生時，最先要報導的是火災新聞。但隨著消息傳來，更多疑問也接著出現：火為什麼燒得這麼大？救援困難在哪裡？居民經歷了什麼？ 大火當天，端立刻派出記者到達火災現場，並在翌日清晨立刻發出一篇詡實深度解讀。隔天開始，端陸續透過深度內容解釋火勢與救援的問題，並繼續留守現場再寫報道救援情況。 火勢熄滅，居民的生活不會立刻回到原本的樣子。到了2026年，獨立委員會舉行聽證會，端持續整理重點，也回頭記錄居民災後的生活。 從當天的火災，到後來的聽證會，報導追問大火如何發生，也記錄人們如何度過大火之後的日子。 火災發生後，我們立刻刊出深度文章，解讀當時最重要的多個疑問：高樓救火為何困難？屋苑圍標是否火災成因之一？這些「複雜事件的脈絡」的報道，被許多人列為端很難被取代的價值。同樣受歡迎的內容形式也包括系列報導、評論和解讀類文章。 跨地域視角是端最難取代的價值 打開端，大家想讀的未必是同一件事。在這次調研裡，住在中國大陸和香港的人，最希望端持續追蹤當地的政治與社會；住在台灣的人，則最想看國際時事。 而當目光落在同一則新聞上，討論也未必朝著同一個方向。 今年7月，香港一名獨立書店店員被警方帶走，身上穿著一件黑色 T 恤，上面印著「我是書店店員」。照片傳到台灣，這幾個字也出現在演唱會的螢幕上。 有香港人感謝台灣的支持，也有人看到自己的處境成了舞台背景，覺得被消費。 端在報導中問：香港的書店正在經歷什麼？台灣的書店經營者，又怎麼看待這場聲援？為何台港兩地互相關心，卻似乎喪失了對話的基礎？ 這樣的跨地域視角，是這次調研中最多人看重的端的價值。超過六成填問卷的人，認為它難以由其他來源取代。 在離散時代，我們更需要這種跨地域視角：搬到新的地方，怎麼認識所處的社會，又怎麼看待原來的家？「異鄉人」是這次調研中最多人喜愛的欄目，也有不少人期待端開設「離散華人社群」新欄目，繼續寫下移動之後的生活。 一位讀者在留言裡說：「走出自己的同溫層，不要再用舊視角去理解這個快速變化的世界。」 面對AI，大家也期待新聞機構說清楚使用的界線 你可能已經會請AI整理新聞，但如果打開一篇報導，內容也是AI寫的，感受會一樣嗎？ 問卷最後的開放題裡，有人直接說：「不要放棄純人手產出。要看AI的話我們自己生成就行。」 也有人期待端試試新工具：「探索AI對媒體的幫助與界線，讓新科技幫助端的理念。」 另有人在意文字讀起來的感受：「希望能够跟所谓的AI味内容区分开来。希望读到有情感、真诚的文字。」 這些留言不能代表所有人的態度，但能看見，大家在意的不只是工具好不好用，也包括打開端時，想讀到什麼。 對 AI 的關注，同樣出現在對新欄目的期待裡。「AI 鑑識與事實查核」的新欄目得到超過四成填問卷的人支持。當 AI 也開始產生我們每天接觸的資訊，怎麼辨認、如何查核，又成了新的閱讀需求。 支持獨立新聞，讓重要的事有人繼續追問 問卷從一個假設開始：如果 AI 已經能準確回答任何問題，新聞機構還需要存在嗎？ 這份用戶調研告訴我們：讀者還是希望有人去現場，追蹤還沒有結束的事。在AI年代，更需要有人查證、交代依據，為報導負責。 這份期待，也反映在大家如何看待訂閱。將近一半的人，把「支持獨立新聞事業」當成成為端會員最重要的意義，其次是「為一項服務付費」。 一位讀者在留言牆寫下：「作為離散的香港人，支持專業媒體是能力所及的小事。今日新聞就是明天的歷史，為下一代留住真相。」 從一家書店的去留，到一場大火之後的生活，還有許多故事沒有結束。訂閱是為值得讀的內容付費，也支持記者再次回到現場，把後來的事繼續寫下來。 如果你也希望，關心的議題有人繼續追問，真假難辨的消息有人認真查證，熟悉的世界還能看見不同角度，邀請你訂閱端傳媒。 訂閱端傳媒，支持記者繼續到現場、持續追問，也支持獨立新聞。 端走到了第十一年。 這些年，讀者散落在不同的城市與時區，在各自的螢幕前讀著同一篇報導，卻很少知道彼此的存在。 今年的週年問卷裡，我們請會員寫下一句話，留給另一位素未謀面的會員。我們把這些話折進幸運餅乾，裝進這個罐子。 打開一塊，收下一封來自遠方的信，也許某一天，換你寫給下一個人。 📍 如何開啟幸運餅乾罐 title: Temu's compliance regime is low-quality, fits badly, and full of holes, says Europe
zh_title: 欧洲称特木的合规制度质量低下、不合规且漏洞百出
summary: 中国电子零售商 Temu 因使用强迫劳动而以低价销售劣质仿冒产品而闻名。现在，欧盟委员会初步发现，该公司还运行着低质量的合规制度，这意味着它没有履行其监管义务。该委员会昨天发布了这一调查结果，指控 Temu 违反了其《数字服务法》(DSA) 的义务，即采取严格措施降低其平台上提供非法产品的风险。 Temu 是一个允许第三方在其平台上销售的市场
content:
中国电子零售商 Temu 因使用强迫劳动而以低价销售劣质仿冒产品而闻名。现在，欧盟委员会初步发现，该公司还运行着低质量的合规制度，这意味着它没有履行其监管义务。该委员会昨天发布了这一调查结果，指控 Temu 违反了其《数字服务法》(DSA) 的义务，即采取严格措施降低其平台上提供非法产品的风险。 Temu 是一个允许第三方在其平台上销售的市场，这种模式并不能免除其对其网站和应用程序上提供的商品的责任。
因此，欧盟官员在几个问题上与 Temu 发生了争执，包括： 要求使用该平台的卖家测试“仅一小部分产品”的质量，然后往往不去检查报告；没有采取足够的措施优先检查已知高风险类别的产品，例如玩具和化妆品，然后没有对这些检查进行跟进；运行审核系统，主要考虑产品是否符合 Temu 的条款和条件，而不是产品安全；没有聘请足够的人工审核员来跟上 Temu 上市数量的增长；当 Temu 发现商店销售不合规商品时，Temu 会针对该商店采取行动，但不会针对可能在多个商店销售相同产品的贸易商；在暂停其商店之前，允许商店犯下许多严重侵权行为，包括销售未通过安全检查的产品。Temu 发言人告诉 The Register，该公司不同意 EC 的调查结果。该发言人表示：“Temu 在合规基础设施和人员专业知识方面进行了大量投资，并实施了一系列控制措施，有效降低了非法产品风险，问题产品的发生率始终保持较低水平。” “我们将仔细审查和回应初步调查结果，并将继续与委员会进行建设性接触。
我们相信，我们将就此事达成友好解决方案，充分解决欧盟委员会剩余的担忧。”欧盟委员会已经与 Temu 发生了争执。2024 年，欧盟官员对其风险评估流程进行了调查。2026 年 5 月，欧盟官员发现 Temu 的流程不完善，并处以 2 亿欧元罚款。布鲁塞尔还向另一家中国电子零售商阿里巴巴处以 5.5 亿欧元罚款，原因是其在制止危险品销售方面做得不够。欧盟委员会宣布对 Temu 采取新行动，援引了《数字服务法》第 35 条，根据该条款，欧盟可以对 Temu 处以高达其全球收入 6% 的罚款，并下令采取纠正措施。谷歌最近透露，新收费导致其来自亚洲客户的广告收入下降，而北京将其电子零售巨头 Temu、Shein 和阿里巴巴视为增长中国出口和整体经济战略的重要参与者，而中国消费者近年来的表现并不强劲。

【原文 English Original】
Chinese e-tailer Temu has a reputation for selling low-quality knockoff products at low prices made possible through use of forced labor. Now, the European Commission has made a preliminary finding that the company also runs a low-quality compliance regime that means it’s not meeting its regulatory obligations. The Commission issued that finding yesterday, accusing Temu of breaching its Digital Services Act (DSA) obligation to operate serious measures that mitigate the risk of illegal products being offered on its platform. Temu is a marketplace that allows third parties to sell on its platform, a model that doesn’t relieve it of responsibility for the goods available on its site and apps. Eurocrats therefore have beef with Temu over several matters, including: Requiring sellers who use the platform to test the quality of “only a very small share of products,” and then often not bothering to check the reports; Not doing enough to prioritize checks of products in known high risk categories, like toys and cosmetics, then not following up on those checks; Running a moderation system that mostly considers whether products comply with Temu’s terms and conditions, rather than product safety; Not hiring enough human moderators to keep pace with growth in listings on Temu; When it finds stores selling non-compliant goods, Temu acts against that store – but not the trader who may sell the same products in multiple stores; Allowing stores to commit many serious infringements, including selling products that fail safety checks, before suspending their stores. A Temu spokesperson told The Register the company respectfully disagrees with the EC's findings. "Temu invests significantly in compliance infrastructure and human expertise and implements a suite of control measures that effectively mitigate illegal product risks with a consistently low incidence of problematic products," the spokesperson said. "We will review and respond to the preliminary findings carefully and will continue to engage constructively with the Commission. We are confident that we will reach an amicable resolution of the matter that fully addresses the Commission's remaining concerns." The EC has already tangled with Temu. In 2024 Eurocrats investigated its risk assessment processes. In May 2026, Eurocrats found Temu’s processes inadequate and levied a €200 million fine. Brussels also sent a €550 million fine to another Chinese e-tailer, Alibaba, for not doing enough to stop the sale of dangerous goods. This announcement of new action against Temu invoked Article 35 of the Digital Services Act, the sweeping regulation of online businesses under which the EU could fine Temu up to six percent of its global revenue and order corrective actions. Europe is concerned that the low prices Chinese e-tailers charge are enabled by forced labor and ignoring dangerous products. EC officials believe those practices mean the likes of Temu don’t compete on a level playing field with continental retailers. The bloc has tried to make life harder for Chinese e-commerce outfits by charging a temporary €3 customs duty for every shipment sent from outside the EU and valued at under €150. Google recently revealed that new charge saw its advertising revenue from Asian customers fall. Beijing sees its e-tail giants Temu, Shein, and Alibaba as important actors in its strategy to grow China’s exports and overall economy, which hasn’t performed strongly in recent years. Indeed, Chinese consumers have slowed their discretionary spending to the extent that Beijing last year subsidized purchases of consumer electronics – including Apple products – to keep cash registers ticking over. ®

title: China threatens 'countermeasures' in the face of new AI GPU rental and export restrictions — Beijing threatens retaliation ahead of Thursday's Xi Jinping meeting, Sino-American trade war may be renewe
zh_title: 面对新的人工智能 GPU 租赁和出口限制，中国威胁采取“反制措施”——北京在周四习近平会议前威胁进行报复，中美贸易战或将重燃
summary: 昨天，特朗普政府扩大了对高端人工智能加速器芯片（即但不限于英伟达 Blackwell 系列）的现有出口管制范围。更新后的规定现在要求获得许可证才能将这些芯片大量出租给美国的整个 D:5 国家名单（禁止武器销售的国家）。不出所料，这一消息像一条龙一样登陆北京，商务部表示，中方“将采取反制措施，坚定维护国家主权、安全、发展利益”。与 TH Premium 一起深入了解：台湾，t
content:
昨天，特朗普政府扩大了对高端人工智能加速器芯片（即但不限于英伟达 Blackwell 系列）的现有出口管制范围。更新后的规定现在要求获得许可证才能将这些芯片大量出租给美国的整个 D:5 国家名单（禁止武器销售的国家）。不出所料，这一消息像一条龙一样登陆北京，商务部表示，中方“将采取反制措施，坚定维护国家主权、安全、发展利益”。深入了解 TH Premium：台湾、贸易和关税（图片来源：台积电） 虽然美国在芯片制裁上反复无常，但中国正在建立自己的芯片供应市场 中国长达十年的半导体发展状况 华为 Ascend NPU 路线图审视了中国长鑫存储的目标，到 2030 年，第六座大型晶圆厂将占据 30% 的 DRAM 内存市场份额 中国最新一轮稀土出口管制解释 美国采取的大胆举措这是一个特殊的时刻，因为特朗普总统目前正在中国访问深圳参加亚太经合组织峰会。特朗普定于 11 月 19 日星期四会见中国国家主席习近平，这次会面一定会很有趣。两国最近都卷入了一场激烈的贸易战，双方的关税和限制不断增加，直到 2025 年 10 月临时休战。
不过，只取消了一些限制；例如，中国半导体在进口到美国时仍面临50%的关税。如果重新启动关税措施，美国股市将出现更严重的动荡。由于英伟达前首席执行官黄仁勋与所谓的中国间谍黄爱丽的浪漫关系，这片海域已经波涛汹涌——人们越来越怀疑这对灵魂伴侣可能共谋从她的新加坡公司 Megaspeed 窃取价值数十亿美元的 Blackwell 芯片到中国人工智能实验室。去年 7 月，英伟达切断了大约一半的亚洲买家，似乎是在出口管制的范围内，并告诉数据中心运营商，他们 50% 以上的业务必须来自非中国公司。与此同时，马来西亚和新加坡都加强了对人工智能硬件出货量的审查。中国的反制弹药目前还不清楚。中国此前曾限制向美国出售镓、锗和锑，而休战协议将该协议搁置到 2027 年 11 月。当这一天到来时，北京很可能选择不再续签该协议。尽管分析人士认为，各国在这次峰会上将表现得足够友好，但特朗普的挑衅行为可能会让中国众所周知的限制稀土出口的核选择重新回到装货区。关于这一特定问题的休战协议只剩下几周时间，将于 2027 年 1 月 10 日到期。
同样，对最新一代电动汽车、太阳能存储和电池安装至关重要的超硬材料和高密度锂电池都将在明年初被取消。分析人士还预计，中国企业及其政府将继续大力投资国内芯片生产，即但不仅限于华为。从广义上讲，美国”更新的芯片控制法规意味着中国企业无法通过租赁芯片来规避现有的芯片销售控制，从而弥补了出口限制方面现有的主要漏洞之一。此外，还向印度尼西亚、马来西亚出售芯片

【原文 English Original】
Yesterday, the Trump administration extended the reach of its existing export controls on high-end AI accelerator chips, namely, but not limited to, Nvidia's Blackwell lineup. The updated regulation now requires licenses for renting those chips in large quantities to the entirety of America's D:5 countries list (nations embargoed from arms sales). As expected, the news landed in Beijing like a lead dragon, and its Ministry of Commerce states that China "will take countermeasures to firmly safeguard national sovereignty, security, and development interests." Go deeper with TH Premium: Taiwan, trade, and tariffs (Image credit: tsmc) While the U.S. flip-flops on chip sanctions, China is building its own chip supply market The state of China's decade-long semiconductor push Huawei Ascend NPU roadmap examined China's CXMT targets 30% DRAM memory market share by 2030 with sixth mega-fab China's latest round of rare-earth export controls explained The bold move taken by the U.S. arrives at a peculiar time, as President Trump is currently visiting the nation for the APEC summit in Shenzhen. Trump is scheduled to meet President Xi Jinping on Thursday, Nov. 19, a tête-a-tête that's bound to be interesting. Both nations were recently embroiled in a bitter trade war, with ever-mounting tariffs and restrictions on both sides until a temporary truce was called in Oct. 2025. Only some restrictions were lifted, though; for example, Chinese semiconductors still face a 50% tariff when imported stateside. A potential restart of tariff-slapping would all but guarantee an even larger amount of turmoil in U.S. stock markets. Those seas are already choppy enough thanks to Nvidia ex-CEO Jensen Huang's romantic involvement with purported Chinese spy Alice Huang — along with mounting suspicions that the soulmates may have connived to siphon billions' worth of Blackwell chips from her Singaporean outfit Megaspeed onto Chinese AI laboratories. Nvidia cut off about half of its Asian buyers last July, seemingly in the purview of the export controls, and told data center operators that over 50% of their business must come from non-Chinese companies. Meanwhile, both Malaysia and Singapore have intensified their scrutiny of AI hardware shipments. China's countermeasures ammo is as of yet unspecified. The nation had restricted the sale of gallium, germanium, and antimony to the U.S. previously, and the truce shelved that bullet until Nov. 2027. Beijing may well choose to simply not renew that agreement when that day comes. Although analysts believe that the nations will be cordial enough during this summit, Trump's perceived provocation may bring China's proverbial nuclear option of restricting rare earth exports back to the loading bay. The truce on that particular matter only has a few weeks left, expiring on Jan. 10, 2027. Likewise, super-hard materials and high-density lithium batteries, crucial for the newest generations of EVs, solar power storage, and battery installations, all have white flags that will come down early next year. Analysts also expect that Chinese firms and their government will continue to heavily invest in domestic chip production, namely, but not only, by Huawei. Broadly speaking, the U.S.' updated chip control regulation means that Chinese firms cannot sidestep the existing control on chip sales by renting them instead, closing one of the main existing loopholes around the export restrictions. Additionally, selling chips to Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand, or Brazil now also requires a license, as the U.S. Department of Commerce suspects that companies in these nations import Blackwell cards to sell to China.

title: Xi personally welcomes Trump to China for high-stakes summit
zh_title: 习近平亲自欢迎特朗普来华举行高风险峰会
summary: 中国深圳——唐纳德·特朗普总统周三抵达深圳时，在停机坪上受到中国国家主席习近平的热烈红地毯欢迎。此次问候为新一轮非凡外交奠定了基础，美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人将齐聚一堂，讨论无核化、伊朗战争以及世界三大大国之间关系的未来。特朗普定于周四与习近平举行双边会谈，然后在亚太峰会期间与习近平和俄罗斯总统弗拉基米尔·普京一起举行史无前例的三边会议
content:
中国深圳——唐纳德·特朗普总统周三抵达深圳时，在停机坪上受到中国国家主席习近平的热烈红地毯欢迎。此次问候为新一轮非凡外交奠定了基础，美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人将齐聚一堂，讨论无核化、伊朗战争以及世界三大大国之间关系的未来。特朗普定于周四与习近平举行双边会谈，然后在亚太经合组织峰会期间与习近平和俄罗斯总统普京一起举行前所未有的三边会晤。这将是三位领导人首次会面。在美俄最后一项核武器条约于二月份到期后，这些会议为特朗普提供了一个实现其谈判新核军备控制框架雄心的机会。他还表示，他打算向两位领导人提出伊朗战争问题。但对具体突破的期望很低。美国官员将三边会议描述为一次开放性对话，而不是一次可能达成协议的会议。华盛顿还表示，它不打算让俄罗斯在乌克兰的战争成为焦点。但据国有通讯社塔斯社报道，普京高级助手尤里·乌沙科夫周三告诉记者，他认为三位领导人在不讨论乌克兰问题的情况下不太可能会面。
特朗普在马尼拉与菲律宾总统小费迪南德·“邦邦”·马科斯在西班牙殖民时代总统官邸马拉干鄢宫度过了第二天后抵达中国。他受到了隆重的欢迎仪式，包括红地毯、鸣放21响礼炮、军乐队和检阅部队。在双边会晤中，马科斯透露，他已要求工作人员安排受欢迎的菲律宾快餐连锁店快乐蜂作为特朗普的夜宵。 “快乐蜂是一家非常非常受欢迎的连锁店，他们的主要产品之一是炸鸡，”马科斯说。特朗普回答说：“哇哦，太棒了。”特朗普还在空军一号上的《真相社会》上宣布，他与菲律宾达成了“新的、完全不同的贸易协议”，他表示这将使美国农民和能源行业的企业受益。这篇文章已更新。

【原文 English Original】
SHENZHEN, China — President Donald Trump received a warm red-carpet welcome on the tarmac from Chinese President Xi Jinping as he arrived in Shenzhen on Wednesday.  The greeting sets the stage for an extraordinary round of diplomacy that will bring together the leaders of the U.S., China and Russia to discuss denuclearization, the war in Iran and the future of relations among the world’s three major powers. Trump is scheduled to hold bilateral talks with Xi on Thursday before joining Xi and Russian President Vladimir Putin for an unprecedented trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit. It would mark the first time the three leaders have met together.  The meetings offer Trump an opportunity to pursue his ambition of negotiating a new framework for nuclear arms control, following the expiration in February of the last remaining U.S.-Russia nuclear arms treaty. He’s also said he intends to raise the Iran war with both leaders.  But expectations for concrete breakthroughs are low.  U.S. officials have characterized the trilateral gathering as an opening conversation rather than a session likely to produce an agreement. Washington has also signaled that it doesn’t intend to make Russia’s war in Ukraine a central focus. But senior Putin aide Yuri Ushakov told reporters Wednesday he believed the three leaders were unlikely to meet without discussing Ukraine, according to state-owned news agency TASS . Trump arrived in China after spending his second day in Manila with Philippine President Ferdinand “Bongbong” Marcos Jr. at Malacañang Palace, the Spanish colonial-era presidential residence. He received a full ceremonial welcome, including a red carpet, 21-gun salute, military bands and a troop inspection. During their bilateral meeting, Marcos revealed that he had asked his staff to arrange for Jollibee, the popular Filipino fast-food chain, to be delivered as a late-night snack for Trump. “Jollibee is a very, very popular chain, and one of their main products is fried chicken,” Marcos said. Trump replied: “Oh wow, that’s fantastic.” Trump also announced on Truth Social aboard Air Force One that he had reached a “new and completely different Trade Deal” with the Philippines, which he said would benefit American farmers and businesses in the energy sector. This article was updated.

title: Taiwan introduces bidding framework for storage deployment at existing PV plants
zh_title: 台湾引入现有光伏电站储能部署招标框架
summary: 台湾经济部 (MOEA) 推出了一项监管框架，旨在促进电池储能系统 (BESS) 与现有太阳能光伏装置的集成。该举措反映出台湾日益重视电网稳定性、可再生能源优化以及开发更灵活的电力系统。该指南于 2024 年 11 月 6 日发布，为寻求纳入电池存储的合格太阳能发电设施建立了竞争性招标和容量分配机制。新框架下，现有并网
content:
台湾经济部 (MOEA) 推出了一项监管框架，旨在促进电池储能系统 (BESS) 与现有太阳能光伏装置的集成。该举措反映出台湾日益重视电网稳定性、可再生能源优化以及开发更灵活的电力系统。该指南于 2024 年 11 月 6 日发布，为寻求纳入电池存储的合格太阳能发电设施建立了竞争性招标和容量分配机制。在新框架下，现有规模超过1兆瓦的并网光伏电站可以参与招标过程。符合条件的开发商必须安装每兆瓦额定存储功率至少相当于2.61兆瓦时的电池存储。竞争性招标机制决定了向成功申请者提供的电池容量电价，引入市场化的价格竞争。获得容量分配批准的项目一般必须在15个月内完成电池安装并网。该框架还要求成功参与者在符合条件的情况下释放相当于额定存储容量1.5倍的并网容量。这项规定有助于提高台湾现有电网基础设施的利用率，并为更多可再生能源整合创造机会。
该框架还包括根据运营要求和其他条件，每日保证计费量与额定存储电量的2.61倍挂钩的规定。放电将根据国家公用事业台电的调度和调度要求进行协调。这种方法的目的是将台湾的部分太阳能电力输出从中午转移到储存的能量可以为电力系统提供更大价值的时间。台湾一直在寻求更广泛的可再生能源产能扩张，同时采取措施改善市场状况。 2025年1月，经济部宣布计划加速太阳能和海上风电部署，目标是到2026年底新增8.2吉瓦的综合装机容量。然而，部署进度比最初预期的要慢。 GlobalData 2025 年 12 月的预测显示，到 2035 年，台湾的太阳能累计容量将达到 31.2 吉瓦，目前预计在 2029 年达到 20 吉瓦的里程碑。政府还将 2026 年太阳能上网电价维持在 2025 年下半年确定的水平，旨在维持投资和部署。能源存储也日益受到重视。 2025年10月，法国电池制造商帅福得宣布计划为台中一个项目提供356兆瓦时的电池存储，到2026年，台中计划装机容量将达到630兆瓦时。
市场上也出现了较早的储能与太阳能发电集成的例子，包括连接到台湾南部150兆瓦太阳能园区的15兆瓦/15兆瓦时电池系统。台湾引入现有光伏电站储能部署招标框架的文章首先出现在《全球光伏》杂志上。

【原文 English Original】
Taiwan’s Ministry of Economic Affairs (MOEA) has introduced a regulatory framework designed to promote the integration of battery energy storage systems (BESS) with existing solar photovoltaic installations. The initiative reflects Taiwan’s growing emphasis on grid stability, renewable energy optimization, and the development of a more flexible electricity system. The guidelines, issued on November 6, 2024, establish a competitive bidding and capacity allocation mechanism for eligible solar power facilities seeking to incorporate battery storage. Under the new framework, existing grid-connected PV plants exceeding 1 MW in size may participate in the bidding process. Eligible developers are required to install battery storage with a minimum energy capacity equivalent to 2.61 MWh for every MW of rated storage power. The competitive bidding mechanism determines the battery capacity tariff offered to successful applicants, introducing market-based price competition. Projects receiving capacity allocation approval must generally complete battery installation and grid connection within 15 months. The framework also requires successful participants to release grid connection capacity equivalent to 1.5 times the rated storage power capacity, subject to applicable conditions. This provision could help improve the utilization of Taiwan’s existing grid infrastructure and create opportunities for additional renewable energy integration. The framework also includes provisions for a daily guaranteed billing quantity linked to 2.61 times the rated storage power capacity, subject to operational requirements and other conditions. Electricity discharge will be coordinated according to national utility Taipower ‘s scheduling and dispatch requirements. This approach is intended to shift part of Taiwan’s solar electricity output from midday periods toward times when stored energy can provide greater value to the electricity system. Taiwan has been pursuing a broader expansion of renewable energy capacity alongside measures to improve market conditions. In January 2025, the Ministry of Economic Affairs announced plans to accelerate solar and offshore wind deployment , targeting an additional 8.2 GW of combined capacity by the end of 2026. However, deployment has progressed more slowly than initially anticipated. A December 2025 forecast by GlobalData projected that Taiwan’s cumulative solar capacity would reach 31.2 GW by 2035, with the 20 GW milestone now expected in 2029. The government has also maintained solar feed-in tariffs for 2026 at the levels established in the second half of 2025, aiming to sustain investment and deployment. Energy storage is also gaining prominence. In October 2025, French battery manufacturer Saft announced plans to supply 356 MWh of battery storage for a project in Taichung, bringing its planned installed capacity on the island to 630 MWh by 2026. The market has also seen earlier examples of storage integration with solar generation, including a 15 MW/15 MWh battery system connected to a 150 MW solar park in southern Taiwan. The post Taiwan introduces bidding framework for storage deployment at existing PV plants appeared first on pv magazine Global .

title: 秦伟平参加德州农工大学MVP国际交流会议：关注科技创新与下一代教育发展
summary: 纵览中国报道 2026年11月16日至17日，首届美台MVP（Most Valuable Partnership，最有价值伙伴）学术交流会议在美国德克萨斯州农工大学（Texas A&M University）举行。来自学术界、公共政策、科技产业及国际事务领域的专家学者和专业人士齐聚一堂，围绕国际关系、科技创新、半导体产业、人工智能、经济合作及人才培养等议题展开交流。 美国海军退伍军人、联邦雇员、经济学者及作家秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）参加了此次会议。秦
content: 纵览中国报道 2026年11月16日至17日，首届美台MVP（Most Valuable Partnership，最有价值伙伴）学术交流会议在美国德克萨斯州农工大学（Texas A&M University）举行。来自学术界、公共政策、科技产业及国际事务领域的专家学者和专业人士齐聚一堂，围绕国际关系、科技创新、半导体产业、人工智能、经济合作及人才培养等议题展开交流。 美国海军退伍军人、联邦雇员、经济学者及作家秦伟平（Weiping “George” Qin）参加了此次会议。秦伟平目前正在Golden Gate University攻读公共管理硕士（MPA），同时也是德州Katy ISD学区董事会第六席位候选人。 聚焦科技创新、经济合作与人才培养 本次会议由德州农工大学Bush公共服务学院（Bush School of Government & Public Service）下属的Scowcroft国际事务研究所，与台湾大学社会科学学院合作举办，是双方持续推动学术交流与机构合作的一项重要活动。 会议为期两天，议题涵盖美国与台湾的国际合作、印太地区发展、科技政策、半导体产业、人工智能以及经济和公共政策领域面临的共同挑战。 随着人工智能和半导体技术持续发展，科技创新与人才培养已经成为全球经济和教育领域的重要议题。会议不仅安排了专家学者的专题讨论，也为来自大学、政府、研究机构和产业界的参与者提供了交流机会。 会议期间还安排了文化交流活动，让与会者在学术讨论之外进一步了解不同文化背景和社会环境。 秦伟平与林佳龙部长会面 会议期间，秦伟平有机会与台湾外交部长林佳龙部长见面交流。 秦伟平此前曾在社交媒体X上与林佳龙部长互动并相互关注，因此这次能够在德州农工大学现场见面，他表示倍感亲切。 秦伟平在个人社交媒体上分享了现场照片，并对林佳龙部长的主题演讲给予积极评价。他认为，演讲内容具有启发性，而林部长亲切、随和的交流风格也给他留下了深刻印象。 对于秦伟平而言，这次会议不仅是一次了解国际事务和科技发展趋势的机会，也让他进一步认识到，不同文化、专业和教育背景的人士之间开展交流，有助于拓展视野、分享经验，并为未来合作创造更多可能性。 从国际交流思考Katy ISD教育的未来 值得关注的是，秦伟平将此次国际交流活动与自己参与地方教育公共事务的经历联系起来。 作为三个孩子的父亲，他的家庭与Katy ISD学区有着直接联系。作为Katy ISD董事会第六席位候选人，他也持续关注学区教育质量、校园安全、教师支持、财政管理和信息透明度等问题。 在会后分享中，秦伟平表示，虽然此次会议讨论的主要是国际事务、科技和经济合作，但其中许多理念同样适用于地方教育。 在一个日益互联的世界里，学生需要的不仅是课堂上的基础知识，还包括批判性思维、沟通能力、创新意识、跨文化理解，以及与不同背景的人合作的能力。 他特别强调，科学、技术、工程和数学（STEM）教育对于学生未来的发展越来越重要。学校应当帮助学生接触新知识、新技术和不同的思维方式，让他们有机会了解现实世界中的问题，并学习通过创新与合作寻找解决方案。 秦伟平希望，未来Katy ISD能够继续探索更多有意义的教育交流与合作机会，进一步丰富STEM学习、科技创新和拓展学生视野的活动，为学生提供更加多元的学习体验。 多元文化是社区的优势，教育应帮助学生面向未来 Katy是休斯顿地区具有多元文化背景的社区之一，许多家庭拥有不同的语言、文化和专业经历。 秦伟平认为，这种多元性是社区的重要优势。学校不仅承担传授知识的责任，也可以帮助学生学会理解不同观点、尊重文化差异，并在合作中建立信心。 他同时指出，国际交流不能取代优质教育的基本条件。认真负责的教师、积极支持孩子的家庭、安全的校园环境，以及对公共教育资金的合理管理，始终是学校发展的基础。国际教育交流和合作应当成为这些基础工作的有益补充，为学生创造更多接触新知识、拓展视野和了解世界的机会。 在他看来，地方教育与国际交流虽然处于不同层面，但最终都指向一个共同目标：让下一代拥有更好的教育条件，以及面对未来机遇和挑战的能力。 从公共服务经历到地方教育参与 秦伟平曾在美国海军服役，之后从事联邦政府相关工作，并拥有工商管理硕士（MBA）学位。目前，他正在Golden Gate University攻读公共管理硕士（MPA），进一步学习公共政策、政府管理和公共服务。 近期，他还参加了Katy ISD董事会工作研究会议，就学区预算修订、建设项目合同及公共资金使用透明度等事项发表意见。他认为，公共教育资源应当得到审慎管理，每一笔公共支出都应当有清晰的用途和合理的价值，并最终服务于学生和教师。 这些经历也构成了他参与学区董事会竞选的背景。 秦伟平计划竞选2027年5月Katy ISD Board of Trustees Position 6。他提出的教育主张涵盖学生学业成绩、学生支持、教师队伍建设、财政责任以及信息透明和公众信任等方面。 从参加国际学术交流会议，到关注地方学区预算和教育政策，秦伟平希望将公共服务、教育管理和社区参与结合起来，推动学校更加重视学生的长远发展。 本次MVP会议为来自不同领域的参与者提供了交流平台，也让秦伟平有机会从国际科技与教育发展的角度，进一步思考地方学校如何帮助学生做好未来准备。 正如他在会后分享中所表达的理念： 不同的视角，共同的机遇，为孩子们创造更美好的未来。 了解秦伟平的教育理念与社区愿景： https://weipingqintx.com Weiping “George” Qin（秦伟平） Katy ISD Board of Trustees Position 6 候选人 Served Our Country. Defending Our Classrooms.

title: Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom
zh_title: 英伟达称被罢黜的首席执行官不会回归，报告收入激增
summary: 美国芯片巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 周二排除了因间谍丑闻而被迫下台的首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 复出的可能性，并报告称，该公司第三季度营收翻了一番，超过 1150 亿美元，超出预期。尽管黄上周因与一名所谓的中国间谍有染而辞职，但他仍寻求复职，但他的继任者、临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)表示，公司现在“一切如常”，因为公司在没有他的情况下仍能继续前进。该公司董事会主席哈维琼斯在财报电话会议上表示，“英伟达董事会一致接受了他的建议”。
content:
美国芯片巨头英伟达 (Nvidia) 周二排除了因间谍丑闻而被迫下台的首席执行官黄仁勋 (Jensen Huang) 复出的可能性，并报告称，该公司第三季度营收翻了一番，超过 1150 亿美元，超出预期。尽管黄上周因与一名所谓的中国间谍有染而辞职，但他仍寻求复职，但他的继任者、临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯(Colette Kress)表示，公司现在“一切如常”，因为公司在没有他的情况下仍能继续前进。该公司董事会主席哈维琼斯在财报电话会议上表示，“英伟达董事会一致接受他的辞职，并且不打算恢复詹森担任首席执行官。”投资者在乐观的业绩中寻找证据，证明人工智能的繁荣能够抵御英伟达的危机，这场危机凸显了据称被中国公司利用的漏洞。 “我们的动力是真实的。英伟达是一家杰出的技术领导者，由我们员工的不懈创新推动。”克雷斯在上周被董事会任命以来的首次讲话中说道。她预计下一财年的收入增长将从 70% 上升到 75%。黄仁勋周二试图重返工作岗位，这是这家处于人工智能热潮中心的公司的最新转折，这场热潮推动市场创下历史新高，并推动了全球经济增长。
最近的动荡重创了英伟达的股价——自丑闻爆发以来，该公司市值已损失了 7000 亿美元。黄仁勋将于 12 月 1 日因国家安全问题接受美国立法者质询。作为人工智能的超凡魅力推动者，他的倒台立即引发埃隆·马斯克和其他人要求他回归的呼声，就连唐纳德·特朗普总统也表示，他“不介意”看到黄仁勋回到英伟达，淡化了间谍指控。 – 人工智能芯片之战 – “自从我离开以来，我看到英伟达的员工、投资者、业务合作伙伴和客户纷纷呼吁我重新担任首席执行官，”黄仁勋在财报发布前几个小时说道。 “如果董事会认为我的回归符合我们的股东、员工、公司和美国的最佳利益，我将很荣幸回应这些呼吁并重新担任首席执行官。”随着间谍丑闻的加深，华盛顿周一宣布对人工智能芯片出口实施新的限制，招致北京方面的谴责。美国新的出口限制和更广泛的英伟达丑闻可能会给特朗普和中国领导人习近平在本周于中国深圳举行的亚太经合组织（APEC）峰会上的会谈蒙上阴影。根据华盛顿的新规定，世界任何地方的数据中心都需要获得美国许可证，才能向总部位于中国、澳门或其他受到美国武器禁运的国家的公司提供先进芯片的大量计算能力。
这些规定还要求获得向新加坡、马来西亚、泰国、印度尼西亚和巴西运送先进芯片的许可——美国商务部称这些国家的芯片存在“高于正常的转移风险”。这些变化是对一个漏洞的回应，该漏洞允许中国公司从东南亚和其他地方的数据中心租用人工智能计算能力，这些计算能力运行在无法出口到中国的美国硬件上。虽然当局已经知道这一漏洞，但黄事件的曝光引起了人们对这种做法的严格审查。他的情人黄爱丽 (Alice Huang) 与这位 63 岁的男子没有血缘关系，是美国旗下新加坡云计算公司 Megaspeed 的前高管。

【原文 English Original】
US chip giant Nvidia on Tuesday ruled out any comeback for ousted CEO Jensen Huang, who was forced out in a spy scandal, and reported that it had doubled revenue in the third quarter to more than $115 billion, beating expectations. Huang sought to be reinstated despite resigning last week over an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, but his successor — interim CEO Colette Kress — said that it was now “business as usual” at the company as it charts a way ahead without him. Harvey Jones, the chair of the company’s board, said in an earnings call that “the Nvidia board unanimously accepted his resignation and does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” Investors scoured the upbeat results for evidence that the artificial intelligence boom can withstand the Nvidia crisis, which highlighted a loophole allegedly exploited by Chinese companies. “Our momentum is real. Nvidia is an exceptional technology leader, powered by the relentless innovation of our people,” Kress said in her first remarks since being appointed by the board last week. She forecast stronger revenue growth of 75 percent in next fiscal year, up from 70 percent. Huang’s bid on Tuesday to get his job back was the latest twist for the company at the center of an AI boom that has propelled markets to record highs and boosted global economic growth. The recent upheaval has battered shares of Nvidia — which has lost $700 billion in market value since the scandal broke — and Huang is to be questioned by US lawmakers on December 1 over national security concerns. A charismatic promoter of AI, his fall triggered immediate calls from Elon Musk and others for his return, and even President Donald Trump said he “would not mind” seeing Huang back at Nvidia, downplaying the espionage allegations. – Battle over AI chips – “Since my departure, I’ve seen an outpouring of calls from Nvidia’s employees, investors, business partners, and customers for me to return as CEO,” Huang said, hours before the earnings release. “If the Board of Directors decides that my return is in the best interest of our shareholders, our employees, the company, and America, I would be honored to answer these calls and return as CEO.” As the spy scandal deepened, Washington on Monday announced new restrictions on AI chip exports, drawing condemnation from Beijing. The new US export curbs and the wider Nvidia scandal risk casting a shadow over talks between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit, which starts this week in the Chinese city of Shenzhen. Under Washington’s new rules, data centers anywhere in the world will need a US license to provide large volumes of computing power from advanced chips to companies headquartered in China, Macau or other countries under US arms embargoes. The rules also require licenses to ship advanced chips to Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia and Brazil — countries the US Commerce Department says present a “higher-than-normal risk of diversion” of the chips. The changes are a response to a loophole that allowed Chinese firms to rent AI computing power from data centers in Southeast Asia and elsewhere that run on US hardware not available for export to China. While the loophole has been known to authorities, the revelation of Huang’s affair has drawn intense scrutiny to the practice. His lover Alice Huang, who is not related to the 63-year-old, is a former executive of Megaspeed — a Singapore-based cloud computing firm under US criminal investigation for allegedly helping Chinese companies procure advanced Nvidia AI chips in circumvention of export controls. Investors are watching for signs of whether Kress will slow Huang’s aggressive investment strategy, which saw him commit tens of billions of dollars to AI companies. Huang on Tuesday sounded a note of contrition in his statement, saying “I did not live up to the standards expected of everyone at NVIDIA, and I have made serious mistakes in my personal life.” The post Nvidia says no return for ousted CEO, reports revenue boom appeared first on Vanguard News .

title: Qué es la APEC y por qué el encuentro entre Trump, Xi y Putin genera tanta expectativa
zh_title: 什么是APEC？特朗普、习近平和普京的会晤为何引起如此大的期待
summary: 香港——在贸易和地缘政治紧张局势日益加剧的情况下，中国正准备从本周三开始，接待 21 个亚太经济体的领导人，这次峰会有望成为今年最伟大的外交活动之一。科技城深圳将成为亚太经济合作论坛 (APEC) 的总部，其主要吸引力将是唐纳德·特朗普、习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京总统之间前所未有的会晤。华盛顿、北京和莫斯科周四确认举行的三边会议将面临
content:
香港——在贸易和地缘政治紧张局势日益加剧的情况下，中国正准备从本周三开始，接待 21 个亚太经济体的领导人，这次峰会有望成为今年最伟大的外交活动之一。科技城深圳将成为亚太经济合作论坛 (APEC) 的总部，其主要吸引力将是唐纳德·特朗普、习近平和弗拉基米尔·普京总统之间前所未有的会晤。华盛顿、北京和莫斯科周四确认举行的三边会议将使地球上三个主要核大国的领导人在乌克兰战争、中东冲突、贸易争端和人工智能竞赛的背景下面对面。中国称这次会议对世界和平与稳定具有“超凡”的重要性，尽管议程尚未详细。除此之外，亚太经合组织峰会还将寻求促进这个聚集了世界近60%国内生产总值和近一半国际交往的地区的经济合作和自由贸易。但大国之间的分歧有可能使这一目标黯然失色，并将经济论坛变成就世界上一些最微妙的冲突进行谈判的舞台。 APEC 是什么？为什么它如此重要？
亚太经济合作论坛创建于 1989 年，汇聚了 21 个经济体，这些经济体约占全球 GDP 的 62%，几乎占国际贸易的一半。其目标是促进贸易、投资和区域经济一体化。与其他组织不同，它的决策是通过协商一致做出的，其承诺不具有约束力。其成员包括美国、中国、俄罗斯、日本、加拿大和三个拉丁美洲国家：墨西哥、智利和秘鲁。香港和台湾也以成员经济体的名义参与其中。今年，中国时隔12年后再次主办会议，并选择了其主要科技中心之一的深圳作为会议地点。在“共建亚太共同体，繁荣发展”的口号下，北京将寻求推动数字贸易、创新和人工智能方面的协议。预期成果包括联合声明、未来区域自由贸易区的进展以及数字经济路线图。然而，关税紧张和战略竞争可能会使共识变得困难。特朗普、习近平和普京之间的会晤有何利害关系？周四的会议将是美国、中国和俄罗斯领导人之间的首次三边会议。
尽管北京保证他们将讨论如何维护世界和平与战略稳定，但三人抵达时的优先事项不同。华盛顿寻求解决核军控和与伊朗的战争问题，而莫斯科则寻求推进乌克兰问题的谈判。另一方面，中国对三方核谈判表示保留，并倾向于保留峰会的经济性质。对于亚洲协会政策研究所研究员李齐·李来说，普京可能是这次会议的主要受益者之一。 “只要与特朗普和习近平坐在一起就可以提高俄罗斯的威望，并可以将对话引向美国。”

【原文 English Original】
HONG KONG.– En medio de una creciente tensión comercial y geopolítica, China se prepara para recibir desde este miércoles a los líderes de 21 economías de Asia y el Pacífico en una cumbre que promete convertirse en uno de los grandes acontecimientos diplomáticos del año. La ciudad tecnológica de Shenzhen será la sede del Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico (APEC) , que tendrá como principal atractivo un encuentro inédito entre los presidentes Donald Trump , Xi Jinping y Vladimir Putin . La reunión trilateral, confirmada por Washington, Pekín y Moscú para el jueves, pondrá frente a frente a los líderes de tres de las principales potencias nucleares del planeta, en un momento marcado por la guerra en Ucrania , el conflicto en Medio Oriente, las disputas comerciales y la carrera por la inteligencia artificial . China calificó el encuentro como de una importancia “trascendental” para la paz y la estabilidad mundial, aunque la agenda todavía no fue detallada. Más allá de esa cita, la cumbre de la APEC buscará impulsar la cooperación económica y el libre comercio en una región que concentra cerca del 60% del PBI mundial y casi la mitad de los intercambios internacionales. Pero las diferencias entre las grandes potencias amenazan con eclipsar ese objetivo y convertir el foro económico en un escenario de negociaciones sobre algunos de los conflictos más delicados del mundo. ¿Qué es la APEC y por qué importa? Creado en 1989, el Foro de Cooperación Económica Asia-Pacífico reúne a 21 economías que representan aproximadamente el 62% del PBI mundial y casi la mitad del comercio internacional . Su objetivo es promover el intercambio comercial, las inversiones y la integración económica regional. A diferencia de otros organismos, sus decisiones se adoptan por consenso y sus compromisos no son vinculantes. Entre sus integrantes figuran Estados Unidos, China, Rusia, Japón, Canadá y tres países latinoamericanos: México, Chile y Perú . También participan Hong Kong y Taiwán , bajo la denominación de economías miembros. Este año, China vuelve a ser anfitriona después de 12 años y eligió Shenzhen , uno de sus principales polos tecnológicos, como escenario de la reunión. Bajo el lema “Construir juntos una comunidad de Asia-Pacífico para prosperar”, Pekín buscará impulsar acuerdos sobre comercio digital, innovación e inteligencia artificial. Entre los resultados esperados figuran una declaración conjunta, avances hacia una futura área de libre comercio regional y una hoja de ruta para la economía digital . Sin embargo, las tensiones arancelarias y las rivalidades estratégicas podrían dificultar los consensos. ¿Qué está en juego en el encuentro entre Trump, Xi y Putin? La reunión del jueves será la primera cita trilateral entre los mandatarios de Estados Unidos, China y Rusia. Aunque Pekín aseguró que discutirán cómo preservar la paz mundial y la estabilidad estratégica, los tres llegan con prioridades diferentes . Washington busca abordar el control de armas nucleares y la guerra con Irán, mientras Moscú pretende avanzar en las conversaciones sobre Ucrania . China, en cambio, ha manifestado reservas sobre una negociación nuclear tripartita y prefiere preservar el carácter económico de la cumbre . Para Lizzi Lee, investigadora del Asia Society Policy Institute, Putin podría ser uno de los principales beneficiados del encuentro . “El simple hecho de sentarse a la mesa con Trump y Xi elevaría el prestigio de Rusia y podría orientar la conversación hacia un acuerdo más amplio entre las grandes potencias sobre la seguridad europea”, señaló. ¿Podrán Estados Unidos y China evitar otra guerra comercial? La política arancelaria de Trump será otro de los grandes temas. Washington y Pekín mantienen una frágil tregua comercial, extendida recientemente hasta enero de 2027, mientras persisten sus diferencias sobre exportaciones tecnológicas, compras agrícolas y restricciones comerciales. “El objetivo clave y primordial es evitar otra ronda de aranceles agresivos y desestabilizadores”, explicó Dylan Loh, de la Universidad Tecnológica de Nanyang, en Singapur. Además del encuentro trilateral, Trump y Xi tienen prevista una reunión bilateral el jueves , en la que buscarán preservar los acuerdos existentes y abordar sus disputas económicas. ¿Qué papel tendrá América Latina? México, Chile y Perú llegan a la cumbre interesados en ampliar sus mercados y diversificar sus vínculos económicos , especialmente frente a la incertidumbre generada por la política comercial estadounidense. La presidenta mexicana, Claudia Sheinbaum, tiene prevista una reunión con Xi Jinping para explorar nuevas oportunidades comerciales. “Queremos que muchos productos mexicanos puedan llegar a China”, afirmó, al destacar el interés de su gobierno en profundizar la cooperación bilateral. ¿Qué puede pasar con la guerra en Ucrania? Aunque la invasión rusa no forma parte de la agenda económica formal de la APEC, la presencia de Putin y Trump convirtió el conflicto en uno de los principales asuntos diplomáticos de la cita . El Kremlin manifestó su intención de retomar las conversaciones sobre una salida negociada . Sin embargo, funcionarios estadounidenses señalaron que no esperan que Trump plantee Ucrania durante la reunión trilateral, mientras China también busca mantener la cuestión fuera de las discusiones. Kiev observa el encuentro con preocupación. El canciller ucraniano, Andrii Sibiga, advirtió que una reunión entre los tres líderes podría alentar a Moscú a prolongar la guerra . ¿Habrá avances en armas nucleares e inteligencia artificial? Estados Unidos pretende impulsar conversaciones sobre control nuclear ante el crecimiento del arsenal chino , pero Pekín considera que todavía no existen condiciones para sumarse a un acuerdo tripartito con Washington y Moscú, cuyos arsenales son considerablemente mayores. La inteligencia artificial también ocupará un lugar destacado, tanto por su impacto económico como por sus posibles aplicaciones militares . China quiere promover una hoja de ruta regional sobre innovación y economía digital, aunque las diferencias con Estados Unidos sobre regulación tecnológica dificultan un consenso más amplio. También crecieron las especulaciones sobre una eventual reunión de Trump con el líder norcoreano Kim Jong-un , quien todavía no confirmó un viaje a Shenzhen. ¿Qué otros conflictos estarán bajo la lupa? Las tensiones entre China y Japón por Taiwán y las disputas territoriales entre Pekín y Filipinas en el mar de China Meridional figuran entre los asuntos que podrían aparecer en las conversaciones paralelas. Entre los participantes también se encuentran el primer ministro canadiense, Mark Carney , y el presidente filipino, Ferdinand Marcos Jr. , mientras Taiwán estará representado por el fundador de Acer, Stan Shih . Agencias Reuters y AFP

content:
Fundraiser by KIMA Network Inc : Flash Flood Rasuwa Children’s Relief Fund
Rasuwa Children’s Relief ensures orphans get housing, food, and education after the floods
KIMA Network Inc is organizing this fundraiser to benefit Kima Network Inc.
KIMA Network is raising funds to support school-age children from Syabru Besi, Setang, Timure, and surrounding communities affected by the flooding.
Because search and rescue efforts are still ongoing, we do not want to make assumptions about any child's family situation. We continue to hope that missing parents and loved ones will be found and reunited with their families.
Our action plan: We collected data from 5 boarding schools in Kathmandu and identified 41 students who are orphaned or have lost a parent, and who have no sponsor or only partial sponsorship. We have decided to sponsor all 41 students for this year and the upcoming so they can stay safe, supported, and in school. The schools are:
• Srongtsen Bhrikuti Boarding High School
• North Valley English Secondary Boarding School
We still have a waiting list of children who need a sponsor. Please reach out to us or support through GoFundMe to help the children of Rasuwa.
We want to be there for them not only in the immediate aftermath, but in the months and years that follow.
For any child who is ultimately left without parental care, surviving the disaster will only be the beginning. They will need stability. They will need an education. They will need a safe place to live. And, most of all, they will need the reassurance that they have not been forgotten.
• Safe housing, food, clothing, and everyday necessities
• School tuition, uniforms, books, and educational expenses
• Longer-term assistance for children left without parents or stable caregivers
Our commitment is not only to help these children through the immediate crisis, but to give them the stability, education, and support they need to move forward.
You do not have to be from Nepal to make a difference. Whether you are able to donate any amount ($) or simply share this fundraiser, every act of support can help us reach a child who may need care for years to come.
Please keep the families of Rasuwa in your thoughts, and if you are able, please stand with the children whose lives may be changed forever by this disaster.
KIMA Network Inc, EIN: 39-4350034

content:
Fundraiser by Yangkey Gangshar : Nepal- Tibet Floods: Help a Mountain Guide's Wife & Children
This fund brings food, housing, and school costs to Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and children
Yangkey Gangshar is organizing this fundraiser.
Our family is heartbroken by the devastating floods that swept through communities along the Nepal–Tibet border, destroying homes, livelihoods, and taking many precious lives—including our beloved first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa Dakpu Lama Tamang.
We are Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering, and members of the Gangshar family whose roots are deeply connected to the communities affected by this tragedy. We are raising these funds for our first cousin, Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and their two young children, who are now facing an unimaginable loss and an uncertain future.
“Cho Cho” is an endearing Tibetan term for an older brother. To our family, Cho Cho Dawa was a beloved husband, father, son, brother, nephew, cousin, and friend.
A Father Who Gave Everything for His Family
At 45 years old, Cho Cho Dawa worked as a mountain guide in Nepal’s Langtang region, providing for his wife and two children. His work often took him away from home for weeks or months at a time, but he took great pride in what he did. He was known for his warmth, kindness, generosity, and joyful spirit.
Tragically, the mountains he knew so well and worked in to support his family became the place where he lost his life.
He leaves behind his wife and two young children—a daughter, 11, and a son, 7. They are now facing not only the devastating loss of their husband and father, but the uncertainty of rebuilding their lives without the person who provided for their family.
The picture attached captures Cho Cho Dawa with his family dressed in our traditional Tibetan attire while celebrating Losar, the Tibetan New Year.
Our Family’s Connection to This Community
Our connection to this region goes back generations.
Our father and his family originally came from Kyidong (Kyirong, སྐྱིད་གྲོང་) in Tibet, a place now often referred to as Gyirong in international news. In 1959, our grandparents and relatives were forced to flee Tibet and eventually found refuge and a new home in the border regions of Nepal.
Our father and his siblings grew up in the Syabru besi and Briddhim communities, where they went to school, formed lifelong friendships, and began rebuilding their lives after leaving Tibet. These communities became an important part of our family’s history and home in Nepal.
The school where our father and his siblings once studied was among the places devastated by the floods.
Yangkey was fortunate to visit Syabru besi and Briddhim in March 2014 and again with Choenyi in November 2025. During those visits, she spent time with Cho Cho Dawa, his wife, mother, and brother and was warmly welcomed into their home. The pictures included here were taken during those visits and are now incredibly meaningful to our family.
The pictures also show places we saw and experienced during our November 2025 visit. One shows a hydropower facility along the road to Syabru besi which has been damanged and another shows the homes, guesthouses, and local businesses in Syabru besi, many of which have since been washed away.
Our family was once forced to leave our homeland in Tibet and found a place in Nepal where generations of our family could rebuild their lives. Now, that same community has been devastated by another unimaginable tragedy.
What took generations to build was swept away in moments. But the lives, memories, and stories connected to these places remain.
Cho Cho Dawa is not the only loss our family is mourning.
His brother, Cho Cho Tsering, is also facing unimaginable grief, as members of his wife’s family were among those tragically swept away.
We are also mourning the many precious lives lost in this devastating tragedy, including relatives, friends, and members of the Tibetan community.
Behind every life lost is a family now facing a future without someone they love.
We are raising funds to directly support Cho Cho Dawa’s wife and two children as they begin rebuilding their lives without him.
The funds will be used specifically for:
Shelter, rent, and household expenses
School-related expenses and future education costs for the children
Medical and other essential family needs that may arise
Long-term support to help the family regain stability and rebuild their lives
100% of the funds raised through this GoFundMe will go directly toward supporting Cho Cho Dawa’s family and, if we are fortunate enough to raise more than is needed for Cho Cho Dawa’s immediate family, additional funds will be used to help other affected families in the Tibetan community of Syabru besi who have lost loved ones, homes, or their livelihoods as a result of this disaster.
Yangkey will be traveling to Nepal in approximately two weeks and plans to personally deliver the funds raised directly to the affected families. The funds will be used solely for the relief, essential needs, and family-support purposes described above.
We want to make sure the support reaches those who need it most and provides meaningful help during this incredibly difficult time.
Every donation, no matter the amount, can make a meaningful difference.
If you are unable to donate, please consider sharing this fundraiser with your friends, family, coworkers, and community. A share may help this story reach someone who is able to help.
Thank you for taking the time to hear Cho Cho Dawa’s story and for standing with his wife and children, our family, and the communities affected by this devastating tragedy.
From our family to yours, thank you for your kindness, compassion, love, and support.
Yangkey, Choenyi, Tsering & Gangshar Family
“The basic foundation of humanity is compassion and love.”

content:
Fundraiser by Rinzin Alling : Help Nepal-Tibet Border Relief
This relief fund directs aid to Nepal border victims via trusted local networks and NGOs
Rinzin Alling is organizing this fundraiser.
Momo Crawlers, we’re asking for your help.
The disaster at the Nepal-Tibet border has left thousands displaced from their homes, and the full scope of the crisis is still being realized. Many Momo Crawl vendors and volunteers remain concerned for loved ones who are still missing.
Through friends and family, we’ve established contact with mutual aid networks on the ground in Nepal. They are also providing us with live updates on the aid groups they’re seeing, what those groups are accomplishing, and where additional support is most needed.
Our plan is to allocate funds according to the feedback we receive from our contacts in Nepal. In addition to mutual aid groups and NGOs, we anticipate directing a significant portion of proceeds to the Nepali government’s Prime Minister Disaster Relief Fund. This fund accepts digital payments, and we encourage you to donate directly if you prefer: https://pmdrf.nchl.com.np
We established this GoFundMe primarily for ease of use and to help us track the impact of the Momo Crawl community. We expect to keep the drive active until Momo Crawl on September 13th, 2026, but donations received now will be allocated to relief efforts on a rolling basis. We will share updates about the use of funds as information becomes available.

Fundraiser by Indian Association of Sacramento : Support for Flood Victims at the Nepal–Tibet Border
This fund keeps displaced families at the Nepal–Tibet border supplied with food and care
This fundraiser is organized by Indian Association of Sacramento.
Please Help Flood Victims at the Nepal–Tibet Border
Severe flooding has left families across the Nepal–Tibet border region without homes, food, clean water, and essential medical care. Their needs are urgent, and your support can provide immediate relief, comfort, and hope.
The Indian Association of Sacramento (IAS) based in Sacramento , California, USA has a long-standing commitment to helping families in need. We have supported more than 40 charitable causes and raised over $250,000 for those facing hardship. We have also responded to natural disasters, including supporting victims of the 2025 Nepal earthquake.
Today, we ask you to stand with flood-affected families. Please give what you can—every contribution matters, and even a small donation can help provide vital supplies and support.
Together, we can bring relief to families who have lost so much.

content:
Fundraiser by Tarra Subhar Massallo : Immediate aid for families affected by the Nepal-Tibet Flood
This fund provides direct aid for shelter, food, and essentials to Nepal-Tibet families
Tarra Subhar Massallo is organizing this fundraiser.
After fleeing from the Chinese annexation of Tibet, many Kyirong Tibetan families crossed into Nepal believing their exile would be temporary. It was not. Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley had become their home instead- a place where hundreds of families had to rebuild from nothing, including my grandparents. Like many Tibetan refugees, they eventually moved on to build new lives in India. However, not everyone left. Some of their family stayed behind in Syabrubesi and the Trishuli valley, carrying on the roots left behind by previous generations.
On August 26, 2026, a glacier collapse high in the Langtang Himal sent a wall of water and debris surging down the Bhote Koshi and Trishuli Bazaar: the towns where that branch of our family stayed and built their lives after losing everything once before. Four households in our family were directly affected:
Our cousin Dawa Dakpa (confirmed deceased) leaves behind a wife and two young children.
Aku Jangchup, his wife, and child (confirmed deceased)
Nama Nangsa Ghongma's family and relatives (missing)
Nama Karmo Subhar's family and relatives (missing)
Now, our families face rebuilding once again, with roads and homes submerged in mud. 100% of every contribution will go directly to these impacted families and the wider flood-affected communities as they recover together. The funds will be spent on various essentials based on each family's needs (including, but not limited to: temporary shelter, food, emergency medical care, and transportation costs). We invite you to help write the next chapter of this story. Please help support this fundraiser in any way that you can.
My name is Tarra Subhar Massallo. I am the granddaughter of Tibetan refugees who fled from Kyirong during the 1959 Chinese annexation of Tibet, and the daughter of a Tibetan immigrant mother who moved from India to the United States with her family in search of a better life. Growing up in a mixed household, I am surrounded by the importance of my many cultures and giving back to my respective communities.

content:
Fundraiser by Dominic Urso : Help Bhujung Rebuild After the Tibet-Nepal Flood
Bhujung’s fund covers urgent food, shelter, and essentials lost in the recent Syabru Besi flood
Dominic Urso is organizing this fundraiser.
Dominic and Kayla are raising funds for Bhujung Tamang, a friend they met while traveling in Nepal before/after the Langtang trek. During that trip, Dominic and Kayla stayed with Bhujung for a few days in his village of Syabru Besi. Bhujung welcomed them with kindness and gave them a truly special local experience they have never forgotten. Now, after a devastating flood destroyed Syabru Besi, Bhujung is facing an unimaginable loss. His home and hotel were destroyed, many of his friends were killed or are missing, and he lost all of his possessions in the disaster. It is estimated that Syabru Besi still has 1300 people missing.
Dominic and Kayla met Bhujung by chance while starting their 7 day hike up the Langtang Valley, one of Nepal's premier hiking destinations. They were looking for a place to stay and found the only hotel in the Old Village of Syabru Besi. Upon getting to know Bhujung, Dominic and Kayla discovered that they were the first guests Bhujung had had in almost 3 years because he was taking care of his late mother's declining health. As a token of gratitude and friendship, Bhujung gifted Dominic and Kayla a hand stitched bag his mother made pictured above.
This fundraiser is meant to provide direct relief to Bhujung as he begins the long process of recovering and rebuilding after this tragedy. The money raised will go directly to him to help support his immediate needs (food, housing, etc.) and give him a foundation to move forward after losing so much. Dominic and Kayla are asking for donations of any amount to help Bhujung through this heartbreaking time. If you are able to give, thank you for showing compassion and support to someone who once showed such generosity to travelers far from home. Please consider donating and sharing this fundraiser to help Bhujung rebuild his life.
